newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas pares gains, still mostly ends up.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas pares gains, still mostly ends up.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, hit by some afternoon profit taking, pared early gains but still ended mostly higher Tuesday in active trade, helped by follow through technical buying after Friday's breakout.

September finished unchanged at $2.374 per million British thermal units after earlier hitting a new contract high of $2.43. October, which also set a new benchmark of $2.44 today, settled 1.3 cents higher at $2.381. Other deferreds ended up by 0.6 to three cents.

"We hit (buy) stops above $2.385 (basis September) and that drove us to new contract highs, but I think we saw some afternoon profit taking ahead of tomorrow's AGAs," said one Midwest trader, referring to weekly inventory data due out late Wednesday.

Despite concerns about storage and some heat in the West which helped support physical prices this week, skeptics said the lack of extreme heat in most regions through mid-month could make further gains a struggle.

"I think we need some new bullish input to see new highs. The status quo doesn't justify these levels," a trader said, noting mostly mild U.S. weather and extended forecasts for more of the same next week.
Injection estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA inventory report range from 64 bcf to 88 bcf. For the same week last year, stocks gained 84 bcf.
And while chart traders viewed the technical picture as bullish, most expected some pullback after an 11 percent rise in five sessions.

Minor support in September was pegged at $2.30, with better buying likely at $2.20, then at $2.15-2.16 and along the short-term up trendline at $2.125. Resistance was seen at the new contract high of $2.43, whick also coincides with the May 7 spot continuation high.

In the cash Tuesday, Gulf Coast prices firmed eight cents to about the $2.30 level. Midcon pipes were up a dime to the mid-$2.20s. New York city gate prices gained a similar amount to about the $2.50 level.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip rose one cent to $2.334. NYMEX said 71,872 contracts traded, down from Monday's revised tally of 76,248.
On the KCBT, September finished three cents higher at $2.25, while deferreds ended up by three to seven cents. The East/West spread narrowed by three cents to 12.4 cents (NYMEX premium).
